lesson_title: Apples and Bananas: Why 3x + 2 Is Not 5x
hook_text: 3x plus 2 equals 5x. Looks fine. Loses the mark every single time. Here is the fruit bowl that fixes it.
clip_script: Three apples plus five apples: eight apples. Three apples plus five bananas: three apples and five bananas. No fruit called apple-banana. That is algebra. 3x plus 5x is 8x — same fruit. 3x plus 5y stays as it is. 3x plus 2 stays as it is — 2 is a plain number, not an x. And the sneaky one: 3x plus 5x squared stays too, because x and x squared are different fruits — one is x, the other is x times x. When you add the same fruit, the count changes and the little number does not: 2x squared plus 3x squared is 5x squared, never 5x to the fourth. x plus x is 2x. x times x is x squared. Say added or multiplied out loud, and the trap closes.
visual_style: A fruit bowl on a whiteboard: apples labelled x, bananas labelled y, a strange striped fruit labelled x^2; counts merge only when fruits match, and a ghost apple-banana is struck out in red.
pacing: Quick fruit gags, a slower beat on x versus x squared, a crisp closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never add a banana to an apple again.
